描述_ZN: Earthenware white tiger tile, Han Dynasty, 19.3 cm in diameter.　　The White Tiger is the deity in charge of the West, and together with the Green Dragon, Vermilion Bird, and Xuanwu, they form the Four Gods (also called the Four Spirits). This tile is wide in outline, and the white tiger is curved according to the round tile, containing momentum and a strong sense of motion, highlighting the majesty of the tiger. The overall design is well-proportioned and aesthetically pleasing.　　The tile is the head of the tube tile, which is one of the ancient Chinese architectural components. It is called "dang" because it has the function of shading the eaves and stopping the tiles from sliding down, which means blocking and shielding. The tiles not only have practical functions, but also have decorative effects. Ancient people often decorated the face of the tile with various animals, plants, patterns and words.
